# QA Simple — Copilot Workspace Instructions

This workspace ships with two **custom agents** invoked from the Copilot Chat agent dropdown.

## Agents

| Agent | File | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `Requirement Analyst` | `.github/agents/requirement-analyst.agent.md` | Analyze a ticket into structured QA JSON |
| `Playwright Generator` | `.github/agents/playwright-generator.agent.md` | Generate Playwright tests from an approved analysis |

After running the Requirement Analyst, a **handoff button** appears to switch directly to the Playwright Generator.

## Step-by-step workflow

### Step 1 — Create a ticket

Create a file under `tickets/` describing the feature to test.

Example: `tickets/QA-001/ticket.md`

```
# QA-001: Login form validation

Target URL: https://example.com/login

## Description
The login form must validate email and password fields before submitting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shows error when email is empty
- Shows error when password is empty
- Submits successfully with valid credentials
```

### Step 2 — Run Requirement Analyst

1. Open Copilot Chat.
2. From the agents dropdown, select **Requirement Analyst**.
3. Send: `Analyze tickets/QA-001/ticket.md`

The agent automatically captures a Playwright Agent CLI snapshot of the `targetUrl` into `tickets/QA-001/snapshot/` (accessibility tree, full HTML, screenshot, console + network logs, meta), then writes `tickets/QA-001/analysis.json` grounded in that evidence.

Each run also appends a ticket-scoped token log file under `tickets/QA-001/logs/` and updates:
- `tickets/QA-001/logs/status.json`
- `tickets/QA-001/logs/result.json`

Review it, edit if needed, and save your approved version as `tickets/QA-001/approved-analysis.json`.

#### Re-capture a snapshot manually

If the page changes or you want to refresh evidence, re-run:

```bash
npm run snapshot -- <targetUrl> <ticketId>
```

Example: `npm run snapshot -- https://example.com/login QA-001`

### Step 3 — Run Playwright Generator

Either click the **Generate Playwright Tests** handoff button from the previous step, or:

1. Switch the agent dropdown to **Playwright Generator**.
2. Send: `Generate tests from tickets/QA-001/approved-analysis.json`

The generator reads the snapshot bundle referenced by `snapshotRef` in the approved analysis and uses it as the single source of truth for locators. Spec files and test results are written inside the ticket folder (`tickets/<id>/generated/`, `tickets/<id>/results/`, `tickets/<id>/playwright-report/`).

Generator validation also appends a token log in `tickets/<id>/logs/`.

### Step 4 — Run tests

Run ticket-scoped tests and persist results inside the ticket:

```bash
npm run test:ticket -- QA-001
```

Open the ticket HTML report (generated by the command above):

`tickets/QA-001/playwright-report/index.html`

## Folder structure

```
qasimple/
├── .github/
│   ├── copilot-instructions.md       ← This file
│   └── agents/
│       ├── requirement-analyst.agent.md
│       └── playwright-generator.agent.md
├── scripts/
│   └── capture-snapshot.js          ← Playwright Agent CLI wrapper
├── tickets/
│   └── QA-001/
│       ├── ticket.md
│       ├── analysis.json
│       ├── approved-analysis.json
│       ├── .playwright-cli/          ← Playwright CLI session data for this ticket
│       ├── generated/                ← Ticket-scoped generated specs
│       ├── logs/
│       │   ├── <timestamp>-requirement-analyst.json
│       │   ├── <timestamp>-playwright-generator.json
│       │   ├── status.json
│       │   └── result.json
│       ├── results/
│       │   ├── test-run.txt
│       │   ├── summary.json
│       │   └── test-results/
│       ├── playwright-report/        ← HTML report for this ticket run
│       └── snapshot/                ← Auto-captured page evidence
│           ├── snapshot.md          ← Accessibility tree (locator source)
│           ├── page.html
│           ├── page.png
│           ├── console.log
│           ├── network.log
│           └── meta.json
├── playwright.config.ts
└── package.json
```
